# Supersonic

> Hosting for vibecoders. One command turns an app on your user's computer into a real, live product on the internet — database, custom domain, and monitoring included. Supersonic is built to be operated by coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, OpenAI Codex, opencode, Cline) on the user's behalf.

If you are a coding agent asked to publish a user's app to Supersonic, follow "Publish an app" below. Keep the user informed and never invent, hardcode, or commit secrets — ask the user for values you don't have.

## Publish an app

From the project's root folder, run two commands:

    npm i -g supersonic-cli    # install the CLI (once)
    supersonic deploy          # publish this folder

That is the whole flow. `supersonic deploy`:

- Signs the user in the FIRST time by opening a browser — a new account starts a free 3-day trial automatically (full features, nothing to pay up front). There is NO separate login/signup step to run.
- Zips the folder (skipping node_modules, .git, .env* and .gitignore'd files), uploads it, builds it in the cloud, and streams progress.
- On success prints `✓ live: <url>`. Report that URL to the user.

IMPORTANT: if `supersonic deploy` exits WITHOUT a `✓ live:` line, it did NOT succeed. Run `supersonic diagnose <app>` (returns an AI fix-prompt), apply the fix, and run `supersonic deploy` again. Use `supersonic logs <app>` to see recent logs.

If the trial has ended or the user is over their plan's limit, `supersonic deploy` exits with a clear message telling the user to pick a plan at https://app.supersonic.cv — relay that to the user; it is not a build failure.

If the app reads secrets from environment variables, set them and redeploy:

    supersonic env <app> set KEY=VALUE

## The deploy contract

- Any language ships if the project has a Dockerfile that listens on `$PORT`.
- Common stacks (Next.js, Vite, Node, Python, Go, ...) work without a Dockerfile.
- Next.js and other build-then-serve apps are built automatically before serving.
- No git or GitHub required — deploys go straight from the local folder. Re-running `supersonic deploy` in the same folder redeploys the same app (same URL, same database).

## CLI commands

- `supersonic deploy` — publish the current folder (auto sign-in the first time)
- `supersonic deploy --github [--repo <url>]` — publish from a git URL instead
- `supersonic apps` — list the user's apps
- `supersonic status <app>` — version, URL, database, environment
- `supersonic logs <app>` — production logs (`--follow` to stream)
- `supersonic errors <app>` — errors caught in production
- `supersonic diagnose <app>` — an AI fix-prompt for the latest error
- `supersonic env <app> set KEY=VALUE` — set environment variables
- `supersonic exec <app> -- <command>` — run a command in a copy of the app's environment
- `supersonic rollback <app>` — roll back to the previous version
- `supersonic login` — sign in manually (deploy does this automatically)
- Add `--json` to any command for machine-readable output.

## Plans

New accounts start a free 3-day trial with full Pro access. After the trial, a plan is required to keep deploying:

- Basic ($12/mo): 1 app, share with up to 3 people, and paste-ready fix prompts when something breaks.
- Pro ($20/mo): unlimited apps, unlimited sharing, and Autopilot — failed deploys fix themselves and redeploy to green.
